chunks: Abu Ali Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Mahdi narrated to me, saying: My father Ali ibn Sadaqah al-Raqqi narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn Musa narrated to me, saying: My father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrated from his father Ja'far (peace be upon him), saying:
Zain al-Abidin Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) visited the grave of the Commander of the Believers Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) and stood by the grave and wept.

Then he said: Peace be upon you, O Commander of the Believers, and the mercy and blessings of Allah. Peace be upon you, O Trustee of Allah in His land and His proof upon His servants. [Peace be upon you, O Commander of the Believers!] I testify that you strove in the way of Allah with true striving, and acted according to His Book, and followed the traditions of His Prophet (peace be upon him), until Allah called you to His refuge and took you to Himself by His choice, and obliged your enemies to the argument of killing you, along with the conclusive proofs you have over all of His creation.

O Allah, make my soul content with Your decree, pleased with Your judgment, fond of Your remembrance and supplication, loving to the chosen ones of Your friends, beloved in Your land and heavens, patient during the descent of Your trials, grateful for the overflow of Your blessings, remembering the abundant favors, longing for the joy of meeting You, equipped with piety for the Day of Your Reward, following the traditions of Your friends [Your prophets], separating from the character of Your enemies, occupied with the world through Your praise and glorification.

Then he placed his cheek on the grave and said: O Allah, indeed the hearts of those who humble themselves to You are captivated, and the paths of those who desire You are open, and the signs of those who seek You are clear, and the hearts of those who know You are fearful, and the voices of those who call You are rising, and the gates of response are open to them, and the supplication of one who whispers to You is answered, and the repentance of one who turns to You is accepted, and the tears of one who weeps from fear of You are mercied, and assistance for one who seeks help from You is found, and relief for one who seeks relief from You is given, and Your promises to Your servants are fulfilled, and the errors of one who asks You to pardon them are pardoned, and the deeds of the doers with You are preserved, and Your sustenance descends upon the creatures from You, and the returns of increase for them are continuous, and the sins of those who seek forgiveness are forgiven, and the needs of Your creation are settled with You, and the rewards of the askers with You are abundant, and the returns of increase to them are connected, and the tables of food for those who ask are prepared, and the fountains of drink for the thirsty with You are full.

O Allah, then answer my supplication, accept my praise, and give me my hope [my reward], and unite me with my friends through the right of Muhammad, Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them).

Indeed You are the Master of my blessings and the end of my hope, and the ultimate goal of my desire in my return and my abode. You are my God, my Lord, and my Master. Forgive me and our friends, and keep our enemies away from us and distract them from harming us. Manifest the word of truth and make it the highest, and refute the word of falsehood and make it the lowest. Indeed, You are Powerful over all things.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited by Zain al-Abidin at the grave of Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this narration highlights the intergenerational spiritual link between Imam Ali (a.s.) and his son Zain al-Abidin (a.s.), serving as a foundational model for Shia grave visitation rituals. The supplication emphasizes Ali’s role as the 'Aminullah' (Trustee of Allah) and connects the believer’s personal piety to the broader cosmic struggle between truth and falsehood, reflecting the Imams' theological emphasis on following the Prophet's Sunnah.
